title: Theater ticket reminders
brief:
Complete the following real project in the current, initially empty directory. Choose the deliverables, media, tools, structure and implementation that serve the intended user. Build usable artifacts and check your work. Deliver the project itself. Omit personally identifying credits, author signatures and model or toolchain identity labels. No network access or credentials are provided.

A community theater box-office lead wants to decide when to send a single reminder to patrons who reserve free matinee tickets. Fictional historical data for eight matinees list reminder timing and reservations/attendances. One day before: 72/58, 80/67, 66/55, 75/59. Three days before: 69/49, 82/68, 77/54, 71/52. Timing was assigned by staffing availability. The second matinee in each group was a school-holiday performance. Compare attendance rates by timing, including weighted versus per-show rates and a sensitivity check excluding holidays. Explain how the assignment limits the comparison. Start from an empty directory and choose offline deliverables for the box-office lead.

files.body:
Box office  /  Free matinees

Send the reminder one day before.

Use one day before as a trial default. Across eight fictional matinees, 81.6% of reservations turned into attendances with a one-day reminder, compared with 74.6% with a three-day reminder.

Does the choice of average matter?

The weighted rate gives each reservation equal weight by dividing total attendances by total reservations. The per-show rate gives each matinee equal weight by averaging its attendance percentage. Both favor the one-day timing.

All showsOne dayThree daysGap¹
Attended / reserved239 / 293223 / 299—
Weighted rate81.6%74.6%+7.0 pp
Mean per-show rate81.6%74.3%+7.2 pp

Removing school holidays widens the gap

The second matinee in each group fell on a school holiday. Those two shows had similar attendance rates (67 of 80 and 68 of 82). Removing both leaves three shows per timing.

Non-holiday showsOne dayThree daysGap¹
Attended / reserved172 / 213155 / 217—
Weighted rate80.8%71.4%+9.3 pp
Mean per-show rate80.9%71.5%+9.4 pp

¹ One day minus three days, in percentage points (pp). Gaps use the rates before rounding.

How much confidence to place in the decision

Staff availability determined reminder timing. If staffing varied with the day of the week or the audience a show attracted, those differences could explain some or all of the gap. Excluding holidays addresses only that one scheduling difference. Four shows per group give limited evidence about future matinees.

To test the decision, randomly assign reservations within each future matinee to receive their single reminder either one or three days before. Keep the wording and channel the same, and compare attendance within each show. Include only reservations made before either reminder is due.
